title: A timed-out submission leaves a run the operator cannot see
description:
'ticfac cloud run uzc' failed with:

    factory request POST /api/runs failed: context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)

The POST had ALREADY SUCCEEDED. The factory created the run; only the response was lost. The client printed a failure, the operator retried, and a SECOND run of the same epic started - two runs writing to one integration branch, which is exactly the collision the publish slot exists to arbitrate.

Observed 2026-09-22: run_cd29a8813c05432a97679230e024f7c2 was created by the submission that 'failed', and run_de249a5660714070be340a647e931d5e by the retry. The first was already ahead - it had cut epic/uzc and recorded attempt 1 of f8l - so the retry was the one worth stopping, which an operator can only work out by listing runs and reading branch history.

What makes it worse than a normal lost-response: nothing in the failure suggests the run might exist. 'context deadline exceeded while awaiting headers' reads as 'nothing happened'.

Do:
- Make the submission idempotent. The client should mint the run id (or a submission key) and send it, so a retry with the same key returns the EXISTING run rather than creating a second. The factory already keys runs by id; the client just does not choose it.
- Failing that, a timeout must say what it cannot rule out: 'the factory may have accepted this submission - check ticfac cloud status before retrying'. A message that implies nothing happened, when something may have, is the defect.
- Consider whether the dispatch lease should refuse a second run of the same epic outright rather than letting both reach 'starting'.

Found while performing the first cloud run orchestrated by ticfac in the container.
acceptance_criteria: A retried submission after a timeout returns the existing run rather than creating a second, or the timeout names the possibility explicitly; and two runs of one epic cannot both reach starting
